Chapter One: A World in Waiting — Arabia Before Muhammad’s Birth
Picture Arabia in the seventh century. Life moves to its own quiet rhythm—out in the desert, you’d hear traders calling out, poets weaving stories, and tribal elders guarding old traditions. Family ties meant everything, and honor was the invisible thread holding it all together. But if you looked a little closer, you’d sense something deeper—almost like a quiet longing, a hope that maybe, just maybe, there was more to life than what everyone already knew.
Now, in the heart of this land sits Mecca—a city surrounded by jagged hills, with the ancient Kaaba at its center. Imagine people coming from all over, making their way to this sacred spot. They’re there to honor their idols, hoping for blessings and a little protection from the storms of life. The city’s leaders, who watched over the Kaaba, had a lot of power and wealth, thanks to the steady flow of travelers and the busy trade routes cutting through Mecca.
But here’s the thing—underneath all that prosperity, Mecca was full of contradictions. The powerful often took what they wanted, while the poor struggled just to get by. You’d hear stories about travelers being cheated or orphans left to survive on their own. The old customs gave people comfort, sure, but they also left many questions hanging in the air. And some folks, quietly, started to wonder—was there more to life than these endless tribal feuds and rituals?
Every now and then, a few restless souls would slip away from the crowds. They’d climb the hills looking for a little peace, searching for answers beyond the world they’d always known. These seekers, known as hanifs, felt drawn to the idea of one, unseen Creator—a belief that echoed the faith of Abraham, deep in their collective memory. Their quiet search hinted at something stirring in Arabia’s heart, something big about to happen.
The stage was set for real change—even if hardly anyone could see just how much things were about to shift. The people of Mecca, proud of their traditions and a little suspicious of outsiders, were on the edge of meeting someone whose life would challenge everything they thought they knew. Soon, they’d be invited to see themselves—and their world—in a brand new light.
